question_text: A group of friends spend their holiday at a beach. Each day, the friends head out to sea for some fishing. Their distance from the shore and the number of fish caught each day is shown in the table: Distance from shore ($x\text{ km}$): 3.7, 1.3, 4.3, 2.8, 0.9; Fish caught ($y$): 5, 4, 9, 5, 2.

subparts.stem: Which regression line should be used to model the relationship between the variables? Explain your answer.

mark_breakdown.desc: Correct choice of regression line with justification regarding measurement precision

subparts.solution: We should use the regression line of $x$ against $y$, since the number of fish caught can be more precisely measured than the distance from the shore.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: When predicting one variable from another or when minimizing errors, the regression line of $x$ on $y$ is preferred if $x$ is predicted or if $y$ is measured with higher precision.
step_by_step: Identify which variable is measured with greater precision (fish caught, $y$).
State that regression of $x$ on $y$ is appropriate.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Always defaulting to the regression line of $y$ on $x$ without considering variable precision and question requirements.

subparts.stem: Use an appropriate regression line to estimate the number of fish caught if the distance from shore is 7 km.

mark_breakdown.desc: Forming the regression line of x against y: x ≈ 0.508y + 0.0615
Substituting x = 7 and solving for y
Correct estimated integer number of fish

subparts.solution: The regression line of $x$ against $y$ is $x \approx 0.508y + 0.0615$. When $x = 7$, $7 \approx 0.508y + 0.0615 \implies 6.9385 \approx 0.508y \implies y \approx 13.7$. If the distance from the shore is $7\text{ km}$, we expect about 14 fish to be caught.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Find the regression line of $x$ against $y$ using $y$ as the independent list in technology, then substitute $x = 7$.
step_by_step: Round to nearest whole fish: 14 fish.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Computing $y$ on $x$ regression instead of $x$ on $y$.

subparts.stem: Comment on the reliability of your estimate.

mark_breakdown.desc: Stating that the estimate is an extrapolation and therefore unreliable

subparts.solution: The estimate in b is an extrapolation, so it may not be reliable.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Extrapolation involves predicting values outside the range of observed data ($0.9 \le x \le 4.3$), which can be unreliable.
step_by_step: Check the range of $x$: $0.9\text{ km}$ to $4.3\text{ km}$.
Observe that $x = 7\text{ km}$ lies well outside this range.
Conclude that this is extrapolation and thus unreliable.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Calling an estimate outside the domain interpolation.
